scope: One missing defendant connected with the Boston Three proceedings; US custody only, existing profiles preserved.

appeal.label: United States v. Johnson, 952 F.2d 565, footnote 1 and indictment discussion: names Maguire and Hoy as separate defendants and records Hoy’s May 29, 1990 guilty plea. Neither was a party to this appeal.

doj.label: US Department of Justice report on Richard Clark Johnson’s clemency petition, Clinton Presidential Library, PDF page 69, footnote 1. Records Maguire’s three guilty counts and 70-month sentence, and Hoy’s two conspiracy counts and 24-month sentence.

upi.label: UPI, June 15, 1994, Irishman sentenced in weapons plot. Contemporary sentencing and extradition report; US arrival February 1994, sentence June 15.

diplomatic.label: Irish Department of Foreign Affairs briefing, September 3, 1996, National Archives of Ireland DFA/2021/50/303, PDF page 8. Confirms Maguire held in FCI Cumberland and visited in March 1996. Its rounded sentence and erroneous arrest chronology are not adopted.

bop.label: Federal Bureau of Prisons public Inmate Locator, checked September 10, 2026. Exact full-name matches: Peter Eamon Maguire 19986-038, released September 29, 1997; Gerald Vincent Hoy 17480-038, released June 20, 1992. BOP release ends federal custody, not necessarily all custody.

transfer.label: Joe Carroll, The Irish Times, January 16, 1997: Three prisoners in US to be sent back to Ireland. Confirms ongoing US imprisonment and approved transfer to complete sentence in Ireland.

final_release.label: Jim Cusack, The Irish Times, December 18, 1997: Government to free nine IRA prisoners from Portlaoise Jail. Maguire already repatriated, with release announced for the following day. The article’s six-years-ten-months sentence is inconsistent with DOJ and is not used.

memoir.label: Eamon McGuire, Enemy of the Empire, introduction, printed pages 9–10, publisher’s authorized extract. First-person confirmation of imprisonment in the US and other countries, and writing the memoir there.

hughes.label: William Hughes, Media Monitors Network, October 26, 2006. Memoir review and first-person recollection of visiting McGuire at Cumberland; gives birth year 1936 and release in Ireland before Christmas 1997.

birth_review.label: An Phoblacht, December 7, 2006, Our Man in Mozambique. Review identifies author as born in Castleblaney in 1936. Month and day not established.

campaign.label: Constitutional Defense Fund, Boston Trial Convicts 3 Irish Activists, contemporary leaflet, PDF page 2. Names fourth defendant Hoy, computer scientist and Irish-American supporter; describes four incarcerated defendants. Campaign assertions of innocence/unfair trial are not adopted as judicial facts.

boston_map.label: US Department of Transportation ITS Deployment Evaluation, Boston city coordinates, approximate historical prosecution marker.

prisoner.name: Peter Eamon Maguire
prisoner.aka: Eamon McGuire; Peter Eamon McGuire; Eamonn Maguire
prisoner.description: Peter Eamon Maguire, known as Eamon McGuire, was an aviation engineer and IRA activist born in County Monaghan in 1936. A separate defendant in the prosecution associated with the Boston Three, he was extradited to the United States in February 1994. He pleaded guilty to three charges connected with an IRA arms-export and anti-helicopter conspiracy and received a 70-month federal sentence on June 15, 1994. His US imprisonment included FCI Cumberland. Federal custody ended on September 29, 1997, in the year he was transferred to Ireland to finish his sentence; he was released there before Christmas. He later published the prison-written memoir Enemy of the Empire.

cases.charges: Conspiracy to violate the Arms Export Control Act; conspiracy to destroy British military helicopters; possession of property in aid of foreign insurgents
cases.convicted: Guilty plea to three charges, April 1994; sentenced June 15, 1994
cases.sentence: 70-month federal sentence with credit for earlier detention. US custody began upon extradition in February 1994, exact day unverified, and included FCI Cumberland. BOP records federal release September 29, 1997; he was transferred to Ireland to complete his sentence and was freed there before Christmas 1997. The 70 months is the imposed sentence, not US time served.

entries.custody_evidence: Contemporary extradition and sentence reporting, a 1996 diplomatic prison visit, 1997 transfer reporting, and BOP’s exact federal release record establish years of actual US custody.

case_research.custody_evidence: US custody begins only at the February 1994 extradition. September 29, 1997 ends BOP custody, not incarceration in Ireland. Foreign detention is excluded from this US episode; no numeric duration is inferred from the sentence.

entries.status_research: Historical release confirmed by the memoir review. Birth year corroborated by two reviews; day/month and death date unverified. No living/deceased status inferred from current BOP age.

research_notes: No technical weapon-building details. BOP federal release can be a transfer, and must not be equated with release from all custody. Sentences are not time served. No photo or personal support website verified. Boston is the approximate historical prosecution marker, not a current residence.
